new_candidates.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim/discussions/919
Originally posted by **junminkyung** October 29, 2026 ### Description When an `OmniLidar` prim with many emitter states moves, every rendered frame becomes slower. The extra cost grows with the number of emitter states. It disappears when the LiDAR does not move. In a CPU profile, the extra time is on the main thread in `RtxHydraEngine::updatePreUsd` → `FSD - SceneDelegate::ApplyPendingUpdates` → `UpdateHydraFromFabric`. It looks as if the Fabric Scene Delegate pushes all attributes of the LiDAR prim to Hydra again, including every `emitterState:s###:*` array, although only the transform changed. The emitter-state arrays never change after authoring. ### Environment - Isaac Sim 6.2.0-rc.14+release.52805.02189a84.gl (standalone, `python.sh`), omni.sensors.nv.lidar 3.4.0, usdrt.scenegraph 7.6.3 - Ubuntu 24.04.5, RTX 5090 (driver 595.99.02), `multi_gpu=False`, headless - `enable_motion_bvh=True`, `/rtx/hydra/supportMultiTickRate=true`, `/rtx/rendering/perSensorTickTlas=true`, `rendering_dt=0.03` ### Minimal repro (attached `isaac62_fsd_resync_repro.zip`) [isaac62_fsd_resync_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34161286/isaac62_fsd_resync_repro.zip) - Empty stage (one 20 m cube), no physics, robot, ROS or project assets. - Four ROTARY `OmniLidar` prims are created with `isaacsim.sensors.experimental.rtx.Lidar.create` under one parent Xform `/World/Base`. Each has `numberOfEmitters` 20,000 and N emitter states (`scanRateBaseHz` 1, `patternFiringRateHz` 10, aux EXTRA). - Only render products are created (`LidarSensor(..., annotators=[])`); no annotator or writer is attached. - With `--move`, the parent's translation changes by 1 mm before every `app.update()`. Without it, nothing changes. ``` ./python.sh repro_fsd_resync.py --out a --states 250 --move ./python.sh repro_fsd_resync.py --out b --states 250 ./python.sh repro_fsd_resync.py --out c --states 10 --move ./python.sh repro_fsd_resync.py --out d --states 10 ``` Mean `app.update()` time over 600 frames, after 100 warm-up frames: | Emitter states | Parent moves every frame | `app.update()` mean | p90 | |---|---|---|---| | 250 | yes | **18.4 ms** | 22.9 ms | | 250 | no | 10.9 ms | 15.3 ms | | 10 | yes | 10.7 ms | 14.9 ms | | 10 | no | 11.2 ms | 15.4 ms | carb CPU profiler, 250 states, main-thread ms per frame (last 250 frames of a 300-frame run): | Zone | Moving | Static | |---|---|---| | `RtxHydraEngine::updatePreUsd` | 6.53 | 0.52 | | `FSD - SceneDelegate::ApplyPendingUpdates` | 5.98 | 0.07 | | `UpdateHydraFromFabric` | 5.96 | 0.05 | | `performMultiTickRender::renderSensorPartition` | 9.02 | 8.58 | The LiDAR rendering itself (`renderSensorPartition`) is about the same. The difference is the FSD update. ### What we tried - **Writing the LiDAR's own transform instead of moving a parent:** prim directly under `/World`, its world matrix written every frame. Same cost. - **Not moving it at all:** the cost disappears, to the same level as 10 emitter states. - **`/app/useFabricSceneDelegate=false`:** much slower overall in our full scene (frame 41 → 84 ms). - **Leaving per-state arrays that are identical across states unauthored:** - `rangeId` unauthored: no change. - `channelId` cannot be omitted: "Malformed model parameter length … is of length 128, expecting length 20000". - **`emitterStatesFile`:** documented as "Not supported, yet" in omni.sensors.nv.lidar 3.4.0. - **Not the cause:** `enable_motion_bvh=False` and `/app/hydra/renderSettings/useUsdAttributes=false` make no difference. ### Why this matters for us We simulate a non-repetitive LiDAR on mobile robots (two robots × two LiDARs). We replay its measured firing sequence as 250 emitter states × 20,000 rays (25 s at 10 Hz). Since #828 / the 256-state limit, 250 is our maximum per prim. The robots drive all the time, so the four LiDARs cost about 6 ms of main-thread time on every rendered frame, not only on LiDAR ticks. In our full scene this is the largest part of the gap to our previous ray-casting backend (~78–80 % of its real-time factor). ### Questions 1. Is it expected that a transform change on an `OmniLidar` prim (or one of its ancestors) makes FSD re-sync all of that prim's attributes, including the static emitter-state arrays? 2. Is there a setting or recommended structure that keeps the emitter-state attributes out of the per-frame FSD update? For example, marking them as static, putting them on a separate non-moving prim, or a Fabric population flag. 3. Is there a plan to support `emitterStatesFile`, or another way to provide a large emitter-state table without per-prim attributes?
new_candidates.title: [Isaac Sim 6.2] Moving RTX LiDAR with many emitter states: FSD re-syncs the whole prim every frame (~1.5–1.9 ms per LiDAR per frame)
